hero.headline: Every task gets its own Claude
hero.sub: Open a task and a session is already sitting next to it — scoped to that one document, there to maintain it rather than to build it.

shot.alt: A task open in the dashboard with the Task Manager panel pinned beside it, showing a ready session and Revise, Summarize, Split and Status actions
shot.caption: The task on the left, its own session on the right — Revise, Summarize, Split, Status.

blocks.title: Four things it does without being asked twice

items.title: Revise
items.text: Sharpen the Why and the acceptance criteria until they say something testable instead of something vague.

items.title: Summarize
items.text: Compress a task that grew a long tail of session logs back into the shape someone can read in ten seconds.

items.title: Split
items.text: A task holding two jobs becomes two tasks, with the criteria distributed to the right one.

items.title: Status
items.text: Reconcile what the document claims against what actually happened in the repo, and bump it.

blocks.title: It maintains the task. It does not implement it.
blocks.body: That separation is the whole point. The Task Manager session loads a skill that keeps it on documentation work, so it never quietly starts writing product code in the background. When you do want the work done, Delegate hands the task to a build session instead.

shot.alt: A task detail panel with its identity, workflow, timeline and ownership fields, and Task Manager and Delegate buttons in the header

blocks.text: The session boots idle: the pin prompt waits for your first message, so you can type your question immediately instead of watching an auto-submitted prompt run first.
